messages:
sam: filing this thread for a weird longctx regression on goliath-32k when using int4-hybrid quant. reproducible on local node.

sam: quick repro command:
```
./inference --model=goliath-32k --quant=int4h --context=32768 --prefill=32000 --prompt=tests/long/loop_prompt.txt --max-new-tokens=128 --seed=7
```

sam: symptom: generation matches fp16 until token +4 after crossing the 32k prefill; then tokens shift/out-of-phase (same prompt, different output). ftok checksums equal.

anya: do you have layer-level rotary dumps? i want to see if phase angles diverge gradually or jump.

sam: attached a tiny csv snippet from layer 12/24/30:
```
pos,layer12_phase,layer24_phase
31998,0.87213,1.23456
31999,0.87220,1.23461
32000,0.87227,1.23465
32001,0.00011,0.00012  <- sudden reset at modular boundary?
32002,0.00018,0.00020
```

sam: so it looks like the phase wraps at 32000 but expected continuity. this is int4h only; fp16 and int8 are continuous.

taylor: interesting. could be packing alignment when k/v blobs cross the 32k address. int4h uses a compact-packed layout and a different memcpy kernel that handles a 64B tile boundary; we saw similar with twitch-16k onboarding months ago.

anya: can you toggle the runtime flag `--rotary-wrap=65536` and `--kv-alignment=32` and retest? also run with ENV VAR DEBUG_PACK=1 to get packing branch info.

sam: ran those. `--rotary-wrap=65536` made the phase continuous on 2/3 runs but still flaky. DEBUG_PACK logs: "pack_branch=aligned_tile (64B)" for most writes, but at pos 32000 we hit "pack_branch=tail_slowpath".

perf-bot: perf regression check: int4h packing tail_slowpath adds ~1.9% CPU on avg for large prefill windows. no mem spikes.

taylor: tail_slowpath could be doing a different index computation (off-by-one) before memcpy. add an assert in the slowpath to log src/dst offsets and remaining bytes. also dump the k_idx mapping for first 20 tokens past boundary.

sam: added logs and pushed runtime branch `rt/packing-debug-987`. ci queued.

ci-bot: [ci] queued tests: onboarding/goliath_longctx_pack_debug, quant/roundtrip-smoke. run id: 20241012-7721.

sam: new logs show at the boundary slowpath wrote dst_offset 0 instead of expected 64 for one vector lane. that's a one-element lane shift.

anya: that explains phase reset. why only int4h? because its packer collapses bitfields and then does vector lane writes assuming alignment; a single-lane offset error will shift subsequent k indices by 1 token equivalence.

taylor: is the bug in the host-side packer or GPU kernel? the slowpath lives in the host memcpy routine (C++) before upload.

sam: confirmed: reproduced in a small unit test that calls pack_tail(src, dst, n) with n==... triggers slowpath and we saw dst_offset mismatch. test attached: tests/pack/test_tail_misalignment.py.

anya: nice. add a fix to compute dst_offset = (total_bytes % tile_bytes) ? and add an invariant check for lanes_written == ceil(bytes/lanesize). then retest.

sam: fix pushed, added pytest that compares int4h vs fp16 for 64 tokens after boundary. local runs show no divergence now.

ci-bot: [ci] run started: 20241012-7721. covering: onboarding/goliath_longctx_pack_debug -> PASS, quant/roundtrip-smoke -> PASS.

perf-bot: after fix, slight 0.6% CPU uplift due to extra bounds check in slowpath. acceptable for safety.

anya: next steps: (1) include pack-tail unit in onboarding checklist; (2) add a longctx-metal flakiness CI job that samples prefill offsets near shard boundaries; (3) update docs about packer invariants.

sam: done (PRs for runtime + tests + docs). PR: https://git.internal.redwood/r/redwood/runtime/+/2467. runbook: docs/onboarding/longctx_pack_boundary.md with repro command and suggested flags.

taylor: excellent. let's backport to the int4h production branch and schedule a canary rollout.

ci-bot: [ci] merged rt/packing-debug-987 -> main (fast-forward). canary rollout queued.

sam: closing this thread, will open a follow-up if canary shows any instability. thanks all.
